candidate_claims: For every canonical QQ1 completion d, the state {u,x,d} is retained, not merely dominating.
The common-nonneighbor set W_d of {u,d} is a nonempty graph clique; it is complete to x,r and to at least one uniform side witness.
For every w in W_d, five repair-corner states I,A,K_w,E_w,F_w are retained while the original reverse state O remains omitted.
For every completion s of {u,w} and t of {d,w}, the mixed bow-tie state {s,w,t} is retained.
Every nondegenerate outer pair s,d and t,u is active in both directions.
collision_audit: The proof that {x,d,w} is retained treats ud nonedge and ud edge separately; in the edge branch it uses an independent completion of {u,w} and a unique later attack at d.
The omitted-bow-tie attack tree treats s=b and s=c separately and skips the otherwise illegal attack at the occupied collision vertex.
Every activity claim is witnessed from an explicitly independent source state.
No graph nonedge is inferred from an omitted family transition.
accepted_dependencies: C-145 repair square only for the ud-nonedge interpretation
scope_exclusions: elimination of the canonical QQ1 normal form
